purpose: Store complete readable English texts separately from descriptions, historical notes, manuscript metadata, fragments, and study commentary.
display_rule: The reader displays english_text only. Attribution and source notes are available separately and never inserted between sentences or paragraphs of the reading.
reconstruction_rule: A gap in one manuscript may be supplied only from another named witness that preserves the same passage. Every supplied segment must identify the witness and source location. If no reliable witness preserves the passage, record an explicit gap and do not invent wording.

readings.title: Gospel of John

coverage.completion_note: Chapters 1–2 have English readings. Chapters 3–21 remain to be translated and audited; the Gospel is not complete.

readings.english_text:
John 1

1 In the beginning the Word already existed. The Word was with God, and the Word was divine. 2 He was with God in the beginning. 3 All things came into being through him, and apart from him not one thing came into being that has come into being. 4 In him was life, and that life was the light of humanity. 5 The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.

6 A man appeared who had been sent from God; his name was John. 7 He came as a witness, to testify concerning the light, so that all might believe through him. 8 He was not the light; he came to testify concerning the light. 9 The true light, which enlightens every human being, was coming into the world.

10 He was in the world, and the world came into being through him, yet the world did not recognize him. 11 He came to his own, but his own people did not receive him. 12 But to all who received him, to those who believe in his name, he gave authority to become children of God. 13 They were born, not from bloodlines, nor from the will of the flesh, nor from the will of a man, but from God.

14 The Word became flesh and lived among us. We saw his glory, glory as of the only-begotten from the Father, full of grace and truth. 15 John testified concerning him and cried out, saying, “This is the one of whom I said, ‘The one coming after me has taken precedence over me, because he existed before me.’”

16 From his fullness we have all received, grace upon grace. 17 For the Law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus Christ. 18 No one has ever seen God. The only-begotten, divine one, who is in the Father’s bosom, has made him known.

19 This is the testimony of John, when the Judeans sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, “Who are you?” 20 He confessed; he did not deny it. He confessed, “I am not the Christ.” 21 They asked him, “What then? Are you Elijah?” He said, “I am not.” “Are you the Prophet?” He answered, “No.” 22 So they said to him, “Who are you? Give us an answer to take back to those who sent us. What do you say about yourself?” 23 He said, “I am a voice crying out in the wilderness: ‘Make straight the way of the Lord,’ just as Isaiah the prophet said.”

24 Those who had been sent were from the Pharisees. 25 They asked him, “Why then are you baptizing, if you are not the Christ, nor Elijah, nor the Prophet?” 26 John answered them, “I baptize in water. Among you stands one whom you do not know, 27 the one coming after me. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal.” 28 These things happened at Bethany, across the Jordan, where John was baptizing.

29 The next day John saw Jesus coming toward him and said, “Look, the Lamb of God, who takes away the sin of the world! 30 This is the one about whom I said, ‘After me comes a man who has come before me, because he was before me.’ 31 I did not know him, but I came baptizing in water so that he might be revealed to Israel.” 32 John testified, saying, “I saw the Spirit descending from heaven like a dove, and it remained upon him. 33 I did not know him, but the one who sent me to baptize in water told me, ‘The one upon whom you see the Spirit descending and remaining is the one who baptizes in the Holy Spirit.’ 34 I have seen this and have testified that this is the Son of God.”

35 The next day John was standing there again with two of his disciples. 36 He looked at Jesus as he walked by and said, “Look, the Lamb of God!” 37 The two disciples heard him say this, and they followed Jesus. 38 The Lord Jesus turned, saw them following, and asked, “What are you seeking?” They said to him, “Rabbi”—which means Teacher—“where are you staying?” 39 He said to them, “Come, and you will see.” So they went and saw where he was staying, and they remained with him that day. It was about the tenth hour.

40 Andrew, Simon Peter’s brother, was one of the two who heard John and followed him. 41 He first found his own brother Simon and told him, “We have found the Messiah”—which means Christ. 42 He brought Simon to Jesus. The Lord Jesus looked at him and said, “You are Simon, the son of John. You will be called Cephas”—which is translated Peter.

43 The next day Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said to him, “Follow me.” 44 Philip was from Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter. 45 Philip found Nathanael and told him, “We have found the one about whom Moses wrote in the Law, and about whom the prophets also wrote: Jesus, son of Joseph, from Nazareth.” 46 Nathanael said to him, “Can anything good come from Nazareth?” Philip said, “Come and see.”

47 The Lord Jesus saw Nathanael coming toward him and said about him, “Look, truly an Israelite in whom there is no deceit.” 48 Nathanael asked him, “How do you know me?” The Lord Jesus answered, “Before Philip called you, when you were under the fig tree, I saw you.” 49 Nathanael answered him, “Rabbi, you are the Son of God; you are the King of Israel.” 50 The Lord Jesus answered him, “Because I told you that I saw you under the fig tree, do you believe? You will see greater things than these.” 51 He said to him, “Truly, truly, I tell you: you will see heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending upon the Son of Man.”

John 2

1 On the third day a wedding took place in Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there. 2 Jesus and his disciples had also been invited to the wedding. 3 When the wine ran out, the mother of Jesus said to him, “They have no wine.” 4 Jesus said to her, “What is that to me and to you, woman? My hour has not yet come.” 5 His mother said to the servants, “Whatever he tells you, do it.”

6 Now six stone water jars were standing there for the Jewish purification rites, each holding two or three measures. 7 Jesus said to them, “Fill the jars with water.” So they filled them to the brim. 8 Then he said, “Now draw some out and take it to the master of the feast.” So they took it. 9 When the master of the feast tasted the water that had become wine, he did not know where it came from, though the servants who had drawn the water knew. The master of the feast called the bridegroom 10 and said to him, “Everyone serves the good wine first, and when people have drunk freely, the inferior wine. But you have kept the good wine until now.”

11 Jesus did this, the beginning of his signs, in Cana of Galilee. He revealed his glory, and his disciples believed in him. 12 After this he went down to Capernaum with his mother, his brothers, and his disciples. They stayed there for a few days.

13 The Passover of the Judeans was near, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem. 14 In the temple he found people selling oxen, sheep, and doves, and the money changers sitting there. 15 He made a whip out of cords and drove them all out of the temple, along with the sheep and the oxen. He scattered the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables. 16 To those selling doves he said, “Take these things away from here. Do not make my Father’s house a house of trade.” 17 His disciples remembered that it is written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”

18 The Judeans answered him, “What sign can you show us to prove that you have authority to do these things?” 19 Jesus answered them, “Destroy this sanctuary, and in three days I will raise it.” 20 The Judeans said, “This sanctuary was built in forty-six years, and you will raise it in three days?” 21 But he was speaking about the sanctuary of his body. 22 Therefore, when he was raised from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this, and they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken.

23 While he was in Jerusalem during the Passover feast, many believed in his name when they saw the signs he was doing. 24 But Jesus did not entrust himself to them, because he knew everyone. 25 He did not need anyone to testify about humanity, for he himself knew what was in humanity.
readings.text_basis: Westcott and Hort, The New Testament in the Original Greek (1881), Gospel according to John, chapter 1. This is an openly identified historical critical edition, not a physical manuscript. Its Greek text is a continuous editorial text and must not be represented as the wording of one papyrus or codex.
readings.translation_basis: Fresh English rendering prepared from the Greek text of the named edition. It is not copied from the KJV or the Open English Bible. The rendering of John 1:1 as “the Word was divine” is an explicit translation choice for the anarthrous predicate θεὸς; the note is interpretive and should be reviewed alongside the Greek wording. The English reading does not add “Lord” where the Greek text says only the name Jesus.
readings.source_note: This is a reading text, not a diplomatic transcription of any single witness. The separate Papyrus Archive retains papyrus readings; the Codex Vaticanus Archive retains its own transcription. Collation of each overlapping witness and documentation of all supplied portions is still in progress. Do not mark the whole Gospel complete until all 21 chapters have been translated and audited.
